subject: Operational disruption briefing and trust-repair plan
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brightgate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational disruption briefing and trust-repair plan

Hi Elena,

Thank you again for taking time earlier. Attached is a concise customer-facing brief that covers: 1) a high-level timeline of the event, 2) the root cause summary, and 3) concrete remediation steps we are committing to over the next 90 days.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Impact window: 2027-05-14 22:06 - 2027-05-15 03:09 UTC.
- Primary user-visible effect: elevated latency and intermittent 503s on inference endpoints serving scheduled batch workloads.
- Root cause (short): a regression in autoscaler-to-runtime handshake combined with a KV-cache eviction race under specific workload patterns.

What we are sending now:
- post-incident-brief.pdf (attached): one-page customer brief + non-sensitive timeline.
- action-ledger.xlsx (attached): owner, target dates, verification steps.

Requested next steps from you: please confirm availability for a 30-minute follow-up on Tue or Wed so our reliability lead can walk through the timeline and answer technical questions. If you prefer, we can hand this to your procurement team for credits/contract discussions afterward.

I will loop Marissa and Irene on operational verification and validation. Expect a detailed engineering note from our SRE lead by tomorrow.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your patience — we take this seriously.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: post-incident-brief.pdf (1 page, PDF), action-ledger.xlsx (Excel, 9 rows)
From: Elena Soto <elena@brightgate.com>

Subject: Re: Operational disruption briefing and trust-repair plan

Dylan,

Thanks for the brief and for moving quickly. I skimmed the PDF — helpful. A couple of items for clarification before we schedule time:

1) Who on your side will be responsible for verification that the KV-cache race is fixed in our environment? We need an engineering contact for our ops team to validate changes.
2) We saw a downstream spike in failed requests to our payment reconciliation pipeline; can you confirm whether any data loss or duplicated responses occurred?

Also our compliance team will want a redacted copy of the timeline for our internal audit. Can you provide one that strips internal hostnames and full stack traces?

I can do Tue 3–5pm PT or Wed 9–11am PT for the follow-up.

—Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightGate Payments

Hi Elena — thanks for the prompt review and the time windows. I'll book Tue 15:30–16:00 PT with the SRE and product leads (Dylan, please confirm).

To answer your questions explicitly:
- Verification owner: Hannah Schmitt (Head of Reliability) will be the single point for verification and will coordinate a scoped validation plan with your ops team. Hannah — can you confirm a preferred verification checklist we can send to BrightGate before the call?
- Data integrity: our initial analysis shows no committed customer data loss and no duplicate deliveries. The failure spike you saw is consistent with transient 503s and throttled retries; we will include the reconciliation request IDs you sent separately in the redacted timeline for your audit.

We will deliver a redacted timeline PDF (no hostnames, no debug traces) by EOD today, and a second internal engineering postmortem for your ops team within 48 hours. Action ledger is attached and includes owners/ETA for each remediation item.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
